question: What are these firms saying about AI in advice delivery, and who is claiming the most?

claims.text: Raymond James investor day deck (June 2025), AI framework: the firm lists "Empower Advisors: Integrate AI tools into our advisor platform that reduce the administrative workload" and "Provide Data-Driven Insights" (instant, natural language access to information and data). It also lists "Safety and Responsibility" with strict model governance.

On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said that in wealth management and other relationship-manager businesses, AI helps relationship managers and advisors search and summarize information. He said this prepares them to deliver personalized planning and pitches and to help with their advice. He added that copilots help organize prospecting.

Raymond James's 2025 10-K (published November 2025) says it uses AI and machine learning, including generative AI, in its technology platform. It also names risks: inaccurate or biased output, security and privacy exposure, and compliance costs that could limit its use of AI. It says it mitigates some of these with "walled-garden" environments.

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published March 2026) mentions AI only as a competitive force. It says an increasing number of firms provide personalized services and enhanced digital experiences, "including the utilization of artificial intelligence technologies and lower cost, computer-based 'robo-advice'". It says this competition has resulted, and is expected to continue to result, in significant investments in advisors, technology infrastructure, digital initiatives and knowledge- and data-powered tools.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the firm is working with a leading AI agent firm on a build-out. He said Schwab can now meet clients' trust needs with an AI-powered capability from wealth.com and will do the same with tax. He expects "new fee-based offers" and cited research that "more than half of our clients are willing to pay for AI financial tools". He also said every sales, service and advice professional uses AI every day in client interactions.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said he would not trust a family's end-of-life financial situation "to an AI bot no matter how good the algorithm is". He said AI should help advisers by producing more bespoke tailored insights and saving them time on administrative tasks, so they can spend more time on personal relationships.

Schwab's May 2026 investor day deck ("Scale & Supercharge") lists AI to "allow reps to focus on deepening relationships". Its listed elements are an enhanced advisor workstation, AI-enabled workflows, and "pre-advice" experiences to anticipate advice needs.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Bank of America's Brian Moynihan said over 200,000 teammates use AI-enabled capabilities and generate more than 400,000 prompts a day. He said over 300 AI use cases are approved, 114 are live generative AI use cases, and 34 of those are fully implemented. He said the tools are designed to help customer relationship managers prepare more thoroughly for client meetings. The 2Q26 deck slide repeats the use-case counts. These statements cover the whole company, not wealth management alone.

Schwab's July 2026 press-release footnote describes Portfolio Insights as a generative AI feature. It gives clients a narrative snapshot of the day's portfolio change, a recap of news on top S&P 500 movers and snippets of Schwab expert content. Schwab states it is not investment advice and that generative AI output may be inaccurate.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Morgan Stanley CFO Sharon Yeshaya called AI "an incredible tool". Her example was AI tools that salespeople use in the equities business. She said the productivity is real and that this is where a lot of the spend is being seen.

Who is claiming the most, going only by these chunks: Bank of America gives the most quantified usage claims (over 400,000 prompts a day, 114 live generative AI use cases). Schwab makes the most client-facing and commercial claims (a shipped AI feature, AI trust and tax capabilities, expected fee-based AI offers, and AI use by every sales, service and advice professional). Raymond James, Edward Jones and Morgan Stanley say less about AI in advice delivery. Raymond James pairs its claims with an explicit limit on AI's role.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (October 2026) reported that Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo continue to develop alternatives sales "along with artificial intelligence functions" for financial advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative. The excerpt gives no detail on the AI functions.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (September 2026) reported that Edward Jones partnered with Aboon, an AI-driven third-party administrator, and Retirement Plan Advisory Group to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool for advisors serving business owners.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative. The AI element belongs to the partner, and this is a retirement-plan tool, not AI in advice delivery in Edward Jones's own words.

adjacent.text: Deloitte's May 2026 research predicts adviser productivity uplift of roughly 30% to 100% by 2032 from agentic AI. It says advisers spend nearly 70% of their time on behind-the-scenes work.
adjacent.differs_because: This is third-party research on the industry, not a claim by any of the firms.

adjacent.text: Accenture research (June 2025) reports survey figures on enthusiasm for AI-based client engagement tools, including 98% and 97% optimistic and enthusiastic.
adjacent.differs_because: This is survey research on industry respondents, not a claim by any of the firms. The excerpt is garbled, so which figure belongs to which respondent group is unclear.

gaps.what: Edward Jones: its own statements on how it uses AI in advice delivery. The 10-K cites AI only as a competitive pressure.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones earnings materials, investor presentations or management interviews on AI plans

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: AI in advice delivery to wealth clients. The evidence covers only AI tools in the equities business.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley wealth management earnings call remarks and investor presentations

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results. The Bank of America AI statements cover the whole company and its relationship-manager businesses, not Merrill alone.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America earnings materials on Global Wealth & Investment Management and Merrill AI tools
